Development and Usability Evaluation of a Bilingual Headache Diary App

Problem

People may find it difficult to recall headache timing, symptoms and daily circumstances during a healthcare visit.

A diary should also capture headache-free days and uncertainty, without requiring an existing migraine diagnosis.

Objective

Develop an accessible English/Urdu headache diary and evaluate how easily users can record, review and summarize their experiences.

Proposed method

  1. Build bilingual check-in, diary and summary workflows.
  2. Ask participants to complete predefined tasks using fictional records.
  3. Observe completion, errors, time and assistance needed.
  4. Collect feedback and revise the interface.

Recruitment, sample size and evaluation protocol await researcher confirmation.

From Signals to Patterns

Daily observations support a conversation with a healthcare professional. A recorded situation does not prove a cause.

Pain ratings are diary measures. The app does not calculate a diagnostic or total migraine severity score.

Limitations

  • Self-reported entries can be incomplete.
  • Patterns do not establish causes.
  • No clinical validation is claimed.
  • Browser data can be cleared; export backups.
  • Urdu wording requires human review.

Conclusion

The prototype provides bilingual diary workflows. Conclusions about usability require completed evaluation and actual participant findings.
